newsitem.title: UK: LME markets favour downside, finish softer.
newsitem.headline: LME markets favour downside, finish softer.

text.p: Base metal prices remained in the minus column during Monday afternoon LME trading, with the markets continuing to cool down after overheating last week.
Traders said copper was looking to correct lower from last Friday's peaks of $2,445. The decline to test support around current levels of $2,350/60 was a necessary "shake-out".
Also, there has been continued talk that China, although needing to buy copper, perceived the market as being too high.
"They (markets) need a clear-out, and around these levels you will probably find some buyers of copper and aluminium now," one said.
Copper spent most of the session nearer the lower end of the broad $20 range, managing to hold above $2,350 but showing little interest in pushing higher.
Spread premiums were also a shade softer, with cash/threes around $80 backwardation at the end of the kerb. Tight dates remain around April/May.
Last three months business was at $2,358 a tonne, down $32 from Friday's kerb. LME warehouse stock data on Tuesday should show a decline of some 2,000/3,000 tonnes.
Elsewhere, aluminium veered towards a test of $1,650 but clawed its way back in late afternoon trading to $1,657, still down $18.
January IPAI inventory data was inconclusive, and had little impact, they said.
Zinc cooled down after the recent strong run-up in values, and continued to display a solid undertone with dips being supported. Last trade was at $1,249, down just $5.
Nickel fluctuated either side of $8,100 throughout the session, closing at the lows of $8,065 after a late sell-off, down $65.
Lead trended lower in line with the overall trend, but held the $670 level. Final trade was at $675, down $11.
Tin dipped under $5,900 to close at $5,880, down $40, while alloy moved lower with primary, ending at $1,545/48 a tonne.
